column1: # Jāmiʿ al-ʿUlūm wa-l-Ḥikam — Hadith 24: The prohibition of injustice

column2: From Abū Dharr (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet ﷺ, in what he relates from his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, that He said: “My servants, I have forbidden injustice for Myself and have made it forbidden among you, so do not wrong one another.

My servants, all of you are astray except those I have guided, so seek guidance from Me and I will guide you. My servants, all of you are hungry except those I have fed, so seek food from Me and I will feed you.

My servants, all of you are naked except those I have clothed, so seek clothing from Me and I will clothe you. My servants, you err by night and by day, and I forgive all sins, so seek My forgiveness and I will forgive you.
My servants, you will never attain the power to harm Me so as to harm Me, nor attain the power to benefit Me so as to benefit Me.

My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, your humans and your jinn, were as God-fearing as the most God-fearing heart of any one man among you, that would add nothing to My dominion. My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, your humans and your jinn, were as wicked as the most wicked heart of any one man among you,

that would take nothing away from My dominion. My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, your humans and your jinn, stood on a single plain and asked of Me, and I gave every person what he asked, that would diminish what I have no more than a needle diminishes the sea when it is put into it.

My servants, it is only your deeds that I record for you and then repay you for in full. So whoever finds good, let him praise Allah; and whoever finds otherwise, let him blame no one but himself.” Muslim reported it.
Muslim recorded this hadith through the narration of Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, from Rabīʿah ibn Yazīd, from Abū Idrīs al-Khawlānī,
from Abū Dharr. At its end: Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz said: Whenever Abū Idrīs al-Khawlānī narrated this hadith, he would go down on his knees.

Muslim also recorded it through the narration of Qatādah, from Abū Qilābah, from Abū Asmāʾ al-Raḥabī, from Abū Dharr, from the Prophet ﷺ, but did not give its wording; he only said: and he related the hadith along the lines of Abū Idrīs's version. The hadith of Abū Idrīs is the fuller.

Imam Aḥmad, al-Tirmidhī and Ibn Mājah recorded it through the narration of Shahr ibn Ḥawshab, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ghanm, from Abū Dharr, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Allah the Exalted says: My servants, all of you are astray except those I have guided,

so ask Me for guidance and I will guide you. All of you are poor except those I have made rich, so ask of Me and I will provide for you. All of you are sinners except those I have kept safe; whoever of you knows that I have the power to forgive and seeks My forgiveness, I forgive him, and I do not mind. If the first of you and the last of you, your living and your dead, your moist and your dry,

were all at one with the most God-fearing heart of any servant of Mine, that would not add a gnat's wing to My dominion. And if the first of you and the last of you, your living and your dead, your moist and your dry, gathered on a single plain and each of you asked for all that his wishes could reach, and I gave each one of you who asked,
that would diminish My dominion no more than if one of you passed by the sea, dipped a needle in it and then lifted it out. That is because I am Generous, Rich and Glorious; I do what I will.
My giving is a word and My punishment is a word; My command for a thing, when I will it, is only to say to it: Be — and it is.” This is al-Tirmidhī's wording, and he said: “A ḥasan hadith.”
Al-Ṭabarānī recorded it in meaning from the hadith of Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī, from the Prophet ﷺ, though its chain is weak.
Of the hadith of Abū Dharr, Imam Aḥmad said: It is the noblest hadith of the people of al-Shām.
His words ﷺ, in what he relates from his Lord, “My servants, I have forbidden injustice for Myself,” mean that He has withheld Himself from wronging His servants,

as the Mighty and Majestic said: “And I am not unjust to the servants” [Qāf 50:29]; “And Allah wants no injustice for the servants” [Ghāfir 40:31]; “And Allah wants no injustice for the worlds” [Āl ʿImrān 3:108];

“And your Lord is not unjust to the servants” [Fuṣṣilat 41:46]; “Indeed, Allah does not wrong people at all” [Yūnus 10:44]; “Indeed, Allah does not wrong [anyone] by an atom's weight” [al-Nisāʾ 4:40];

and “Whoever does righteous deeds while a believer will fear neither injustice nor deprivation” [Ṭā Hā 20:112]. Deprivation (haḍm) is having the reward of one's good deeds reduced, and injustice is being punished for the sins of others. There is much like this in the Qurʾān.
This is among what shows that Allah is able to do injustice, but does not do it, out of His grace and generosity, His nobility and His kindness to His servants.
Many scholars have explained injustice as putting things where they do not belong.

As for those who explained it as disposing of what belongs to another without his permission — and something like this is reported from Iyās ibn Muʿāwiyah and others — they say that injustice is impossible for Him and inconceivable in His case,
The printed text reads وغيرُه متصوَّر, which contradicts the argument; read وغيرُ متصوَّر (“and inconceivable”), as in Ibn Rajab's Tafsīr, which repeats the passage.
because everything He does is disposing of what is His own. Abū al-Aswad al-Duʾalī answered ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn in a similar way when he asked him about the decree.

Abū Dāwūd and Ibn Mājah recorded, from the hadith of Abū Sinān Saʿīd ibn Sinān, from Wahb ibn Khālid al-Ḥimṣī, from Ibn al-Daylamī, that he heard Ubayy ibn Kaʿb say: If Allah punished the inhabitants of His heavens and the inhabitants of His earth,

He would punish them without being unjust to them; and if He had mercy on them, His mercy would be better for them than their deeds. And Ibn al-Daylamī went to Ibn Masʿūd, who told him the same, and then went to Zayd ibn Thābit, who narrated the same to him from the Prophet ﷺ.
This hadith is open to question; Wahb ibn Khālid is not particularly well known for knowledge.
It may be understood to mean that, were He to will to punish them, He would decree for them what He would punish them for, and so He would not then be unjust to them.

That He created the deeds of His servants, injustice among them, does not entail describing Him — Glorified and Exalted is He — as unjust, just as He is not described by any of the other evil deeds His servants commit, though they are His creation and His decree;

for He is described only by His own acts, not by the acts of His servants. His servants' acts are things He has created and brought about, and He is not described by any of them; He is described only by the attributes and acts that subsist in Him. And Allah knows best.

His words, “And have made it forbidden among you, so do not wrong one another,” mean that the Exalted has forbidden injustice to His servants and prohibited them from wronging one another. So it is unlawful for any servant to wrong another — though injustice in itself is unlawful in every case. It is of two kinds.

The first is wronging oneself, the greatest form of which is shirk, as the Exalted said: “Indeed, shirk is a great injustice” [Luqmān 31:13]. For the one who associates partners puts a created thing in the place of the Creator, worshipping it and taking it as a god, and so puts things where they do not belong.

Most of the threats against wrongdoers mentioned in the Qurʾān are meant for the idolaters, as Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: “And the disbelievers — they are the wrongdoers” [al-Baqarah 2:254]. After that come sins of all their various kinds, major and minor.

The second is a servant's wronging others, and this is what is mentioned in this hadith. The Prophet ﷺ said in his sermon during the Farewell Pilgrimage: “Your blood, your wealth and your honour are sacred to you, as sacred as this day of yours, in this month of yours, in this land of yours.”
It is narrated that he gave this sermon on the day of ʿArafah, on the Day of Sacrifice and on the second of the days of Tashrīq. In one narration, he then said:
“Listen to me and you will live. Indeed, do no wrong; indeed, do no wrong; indeed, do no wrong. The wealth of a Muslim is not lawful except with his willing consent.”
In the two Ṣaḥīḥs, from Ibn ʿUmar, the Prophet ﷺ said: “Injustice will be darknesses on the Day of Resurrection.”

Both have, from Abū Mūsā, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Allah gives the wrongdoer respite, but when He seizes him He does not let him escape.” Then he recited: “Such is the seizing of your Lord when He seizes the towns while they are doing wrong; indeed, His seizing is painful and severe” [Hūd 11:102].
In Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, from Abū Hurayrah, the Prophet ﷺ said: “Whoever has wronged his brother in some way, let him seek his pardon for it now,

for there will be neither dīnār nor dirham there, before some of his good deeds are taken and given to his brother; and if he has no good deeds, some of his brother's bad deeds will be taken and thrown upon him.”

His words: “My servants, all of you are astray except those I have guided, so seek guidance from Me and I will guide you. My servants, all of you are hungry except those I have fed, so seek food from Me and I will feed you. My servants,

all of you are naked except those I have clothed, so seek clothing from Me and I will clothe you. My servants, you err by night and by day, and I forgive all sins, so seek My forgiveness and I will forgive you.”

This entails that all creation depends on Allah the Exalted to secure their interests and ward off what harms them in the affairs of their religion and their worldly life, and that the servants have no power over any of that for themselves;

and that whoever Allah does not favour with guidance and provision is deprived of both in this world, and whoever Allah does not favour with the forgiveness of his sins is ruined by his wrongdoings in the Hereafter.

Allah the Exalted said: “Whoever Allah guides is rightly guided, and whoever He sends astray — you will never find for him a protector to guide him” [al-Kahf 18:17]. There is much like this in the Qurʾān. The Exalted said: “Whatever mercy Allah opens to people, none can withhold it; and whatever He withholds, none can release it after Him” [Fāṭir 35:2];

and: “Indeed, Allah is the Provider, the Possessor of strength, the Firm” [al-Dhāriyāt 51:58]; and: “So seek provision from Allah and worship Him” [al-ʿAnkabūt 29:17]; and: “There is no creature on earth but its provision rests with Allah” [Hūd 11:6].

The Exalted said, relating that Ādam and his wife said: “Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves; if You do not forgive us and have mercy on us, we will surely be among the losers” [al-Aʿrāf 7:23]; and of Nūḥ (blessings and peace be upon him) that he said: “And unless You forgive me and have mercy on me, I will be among the losers” [Hūd 11:47].

Ibrāhīm, the Friend of Allah (peace be upon him), argued from Allah's being alone in doing these things that there is no god but Him, and that whatever is associated with Him is false. He said to his people:

“Have you considered what you have been worshipping — you and your forefathers? They are enemies to me, except the Lord of the worlds, who created me, and it is He who guides me; who feeds me and gives me drink; and when I am ill, it is He who cures me; who will cause me to die and then bring me to life; and who, I hope, will forgive me my sins on the Day of Judgement” [al-Shuʿarāʾ 26:75–82].

For the One who alone creates the servant, guides him, provides for him, gives him life and death in this world, and forgives his sins in the Hereafter, deserves to be singled out with divinity and worship, with asking and humble entreaty, and with submission.

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: “Allah is the One who created you, then provided for you, then will cause you to die, then will give you life. Is there any of your partners who does any of that? Glorified and Exalted is He above what they associate with Him” [al-Rūm 30:40].

The hadith is evidence that Allah loves His servants to ask Him for all the interests of their religion and their worldly life — food, drink, clothing and so on — just as they ask Him for guidance and forgiveness. In the hadith: “Let each of you ask his Lord for all his needs — even for the strap of his sandal when it breaks.”
One of the Salaf used to ask Allah in his prayer for all his needs, even the salt for his dough and the fodder for his sheep.

In the Isrāʾīliyyāt it is related that Mūsā (peace be upon him) said: Lord, some worldly need comes up for me and I feel too shy to ask You. He said: Ask Me, even for the salt for your dough and the fodder for your donkey.

For whenever a servant asks Allah for anything he needs, he shows his need in it and his dependence on Allah, and Allah loves that. One of the Salaf used to feel too shy before Allah to ask Him for anything of worldly benefit, but following the Sunnah is better.
His words, “All of you are astray except those I have guided”: some have thought this conflicts with the hadith of ʿIyāḍ ibn Ḥimār from the Prophet ﷺ:

“Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: I created My servants upright in faith (ḥunafāʾ)” — and in one narration, “Muslims” — “and then the devils led them astray.” But it is not so. Allah created the children of Ādam and gave them a natural disposition (fiṭrah) to accept Islam,

to incline to it rather than to anything else, and to be ready and prepared for it in potential. But the servant still needs actually to be taught Islam, for before he is taught he is ignorant and knows nothing,
as the Mighty and Majestic said: “And Allah brought you out of your mothers' wombs knowing nothing” [al-Naḥl 16:78]; and He said to His Prophet ﷺ:

“And He found you astray and guided you” [al-Ḍuḥā 93:7] — meaning, He found you without knowledge of the Book and wisdom that He then taught you, as the Exalted said: “And thus We revealed to you a spirit of Our command; you did not know what the Book was, nor faith” [al-Shūrā 42:52]. So a person is born with a natural disposition to accept the truth.
If Allah guides him, He provides him with someone to teach him guidance, and he becomes guided in fact after having been guided in potential; and if Allah forsakes him,
He assigns him someone who teaches him what alters his natural disposition, as he ﷺ said: “Every child is born upon the fiṭrah; then his parents make him a Jew, a Christian or a Magian.”

As for the believer asking Allah for guidance: guidance is of two kinds. There is general guidance, which is guidance to Islam and faith, and this the believer already has; and there is detailed guidance, which is being guided to know the details of the parts of faith and Islam

and being helped to carry them out. Every believer needs this night and day, which is why Allah commanded His servants to recite in every rakʿah of their prayer His words: “Guide us to the straight path” [al-Fātiḥah 1:6].

The Prophet ﷺ used to say in his supplication at night: “Guide me, by Your leave, to the truth in what has been disputed; indeed, You guide whom You will to a straight path.” That is also why, when one who sneezes is answered, he is told

“May Allah have mercy on you,” and he replies, “May Allah guide you,” as the Sunnah has it — even though some of the jurists of Iraq objected to it, thinking that a Muslim does not need to be prayed for to be guided. The majority of scholars differed with them, following the Sunnah in this.
The Prophet ﷺ commanded ʿAlī to ask Allah for right aim and guidance, and taught al-Ḥasan to say in the qunūt of the witr: “O Allah, guide me among those You have guided.”
As for seeking forgiveness for sins: it is asking for forgiveness, and the servant needs it more than anything,

because he errs night and day. Repentance and seeking forgiveness are mentioned again and again in the Qurʾān, with commands to do them and encouragement towards them. Al-Tirmidhī and Ibn Mājah recorded, from the hadith of Anas, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Every son of Ādam errs greatly, and the best of those who err are those who repent much.”
Al-Bukhārī recorded, from the hadith of Abū Hurayrah, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “By Allah, I seek Allah's forgiveness and repent to Him more than seventy times a day.”
Al-Nasāʾī and Ibn Mājah recorded it in the wording: “I seek Allah's forgiveness and repent to Him a hundred times every day.”
Muslim recorded, from the hadith of al-Agharr al-Muzanī, that he heard the Prophet ﷺ say: “O people, repent to your Lord,

for I repent to Him a hundred times a day.” Al-Nasāʾī recorded it in the wording: “O people, repent to your Lord and seek His forgiveness, for I repent to Allah and seek His forgiveness a hundred times every day.”

Imam Aḥmad recorded, from the hadith of Ḥudhayfah, who said: My tongue was sharp with my family, though it went no further than them. I mentioned that to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: “What keeps you from seeking forgiveness, Ḥudhayfah? I seek Allah's forgiveness a hundred times every day.”
And from the hadith of Abū Mūsā, the Prophet ﷺ said: “I seek Allah's forgiveness a hundred times every day and repent to Him.”
Al-Nasāʾī recorded, from the hadith of Abū Mūsā, who said: We were sitting when the Prophet ﷺ came and said: “I have never begun a morning without seeking Allah's forgiveness a hundred times.”
Imam Aḥmad, Abū Dāwūd, al-Tirmidhī, al-Nasāʾī and Ibn Mājah recorded, from the hadith of Ibn ʿUmar, who said:
We used to count for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, in a single sitting, a hundred times his saying: “My Lord, forgive me and accept my repentance; You are the Accepter of Repentance, the Most Merciful.”
Al-Nasāʾī recorded, from the hadith of Abū Hurayrah, who said: I have seen no one say “I seek Allah's forgiveness and repent to Him” more often than the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

Imam Aḥmad recorded, from the hadith of ʿĀʾishah, that the Prophet ﷺ used to say: “O Allah, make me one of those who, when they do good, rejoice, and when they do wrong, seek forgiveness.” We shall say more about seeking forgiveness later, if Allah the Exalted wills.

His words, “My servants, you will never attain the power to harm Me so as to harm Me, nor attain the power to benefit Me so as to benefit Me,” mean that the servants cannot bring any benefit or harm to Allah. For Allah the Exalted is in Himself Rich and Praiseworthy;

He has no need of His servants' acts of obedience, and their benefit does not go back to Him — it is they who benefit from them; nor is He harmed by their sins — it is they who are harmed by them. Allah the Exalted said: “And do not let those who hasten into disbelief grieve you; they will never harm Allah at all” [Āl ʿImrān 3:176].
And He said: “And whoever turns back on his heels will not harm Allah at all” [Āl ʿImrān 3:144].
The Prophet ﷺ used to say in his sermon: “And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger has gone astray; he harms only himself, and does not harm Allah at all.”

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: “And if you disbelieve, then to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and Allah is Rich, Praiseworthy” [al-Nisāʾ 4:131]. Relating of Mūsā, He said:

“And Mūsā said: If you disbelieve, you and all who are on the earth, Allah is Rich, Praiseworthy” [Ibrāhīm 14:8]. And He said: “And whoever disbelieves — Allah has no need of the worlds” [Āl ʿImrān 3:97]. And He said: “Their flesh and their blood do not reach Allah, but what reaches Him is the taqwā from you” [al-Ḥajj 22:37].

The meaning is that the Exalted loves His servants to fear Him and obey Him, just as He dislikes their disobeying Him. That is why He rejoices at the repentance of those who repent more than a man rejoices who loses, in a waterless desert, the mount that carries his food and drink,

searches for it until he is exhausted and gives up hope of it, resigns himself to death and despairs of life, and then is overcome by sleep; and when he wakes, there it is, standing beside him. This is the greatest joy a creature can imagine — all this while He has no need of His servants' obedience and their repentance to Him,
and their benefit goes only to them, not to Him. Rather, it comes from the perfection of His generosity and kindness to His servants, and His love of benefiting them and warding off harm from them.
He loves His servants to know Him, love Him, fear Him, be mindful of Him, obey Him and draw near to Him; and He loves them to know that none forgives sins but He,

and that He is able to forgive His servants' sins, as in ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ghanm's narration of this hadith from Abū Dharr: “Whoever of you knows that I have the power to forgive and then seeks My forgiveness, I forgive him, and I do not mind.”

In the Ṣaḥīḥ, the Prophet ﷺ said: “A servant committed a sin and said: Lord, I have committed a sin, so forgive me. Allah said: My servant knows that he has a Lord who forgives sin and takes to account for sin; I have forgiven My servant.”

In the hadith of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, when the Prophet ﷺ mounted his riding animal he praised Allah three times and said Allāhu akbar three times, and said: “Glory be to You! I have wronged myself, so forgive me,

for none forgives sins but You.” Then he laughed and said: “Your Lord marvels at His servant when he says, ‘My Lord, forgive me my sins’ — he knows that none forgives sins but Me.” Imam Aḥmad and al-Tirmidhī recorded it, and al-Tirmidhī declared it authentic.
In the Ṣaḥīḥ, the Prophet ﷺ said: “By Allah, Allah is more merciful to His servants than a mother to her child.”
One of the companions of Dhū al-Nūn used to go about calling out: Ah, where is my heart? Who has found my heart?

One day he entered a certain lane and found a boy crying while his mother beat him. Then she put him out of the house and shut the door on him. The boy began looking right and left, not knowing where to go or where to turn.
He came back to the door of the house and began crying and saying: Mother, who will open the door for me if you shut your door on me?
Who will draw me close if you drive me away?
Who will draw me near after you have been angry with me?

His mother took pity on him; she got up and looked through a gap in the door, and found her son with tears running down his cheeks, rolling in the dust. She opened the door, took him up and set him in her lap, and began kissing him and saying: Delight of my eyes, dear to my soul,

it was you who provoked me against yourself, and you who brought on yourself what befell you; had you obeyed me, you would have met nothing unpleasant from me. The young man was overcome with ecstasy; he rose, cried out and said: I have found my heart, I have found my heart!

Reflect on His words: “And those who, when they commit an indecency or wrong themselves, remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins — and who forgives sins except Allah?” [Āl ʿImrān 3:135]. They indicate that sinners have no one but Him to turn to for refuge and to rely on for the forgiveness of their sins.

Likewise His words concerning the three who were left behind: “Until, when the earth, vast as it is, closed in on them, and their souls closed in on them, and they were certain that there is no refuge from Allah except in Him, He turned to them so that they might repent; indeed, Allah is the Accepter of Repentance, the Most Merciful” [al-Tawbah 9:118].

He made His turning to them follow their certainty that there was no refuge from Allah except in Him. For when a servant fears a created being, he flees from him to someone else; but whoever fears Allah has no refuge to take refuge in

and no place of flight to flee to except Him, so he flees from Him to Him — as the Prophet ﷺ used to say in his supplication: “There is no refuge and no escape from You except to You”; and he used to say: “I seek refuge in Your good pleasure from Your anger, in Your pardon from Your punishment, and in You from You.”

Al-Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ (may Allah have mercy on him) said: There is no night whose darkness has gathered and which has let down the robe of its covering, but the Majestic, Majestic is His majesty, calls out: Who is greater than I in generosity, when creatures disobey Me

and I watch over them, guarding them in their beds as though they had not disobeyed Me, and taking charge of protecting them as though they had committed no sin between Me and them? I am generous with My bounty to the disobedient and bestow favour on the wrongdoer. Who is it that called on Me and I did not answer him?
Or who is it that asked of Me and I did not give him?
Or who is it that made his camel kneel at My door and I sent him away?

I am bounty, and from Me comes bounty; I am the Generous, and from Me comes generosity; I am the Noble, and from Me comes nobility. It is of My nobility that I forgive the disobedient after their disobedience;

it is of My nobility that I give the servant what he asked of Me and give him what he did not ask; and it is of My nobility that I give the one who repents as though he had never disobeyed Me. So where can creatures flee from Me?
And where can the disobedient turn away from My door?
Abū Nuʿaym recorded it.
Someone wrote on this theme:
I did wrong and did no good, and I have come to You repenting — / and where can a slave flee from his masters?
He hopes for forgiveness; and if his hope is dashed, / no one on earth is more disappointed than he.

So His words after this — “My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, your humans and your jinn, were as God-fearing as the most God-fearing heart of any one man among you, that would add nothing to My dominion;

and if they were as wicked as the most wicked heart of any one man among you, that would take nothing away from My dominion” — indicate that His dominion does not increase through the obedience of creation, even if they were all righteous and God-fearing,

their hearts like the heart of the most God-fearing man among them; nor does His dominion decrease through the disobedience of the disobedient, even if jinn and humans were all disobedient and wicked, their hearts like the heart of the most wicked man among them.

For He, Glorified is He, is in Himself free of need of all besides Him, and He has absolute perfection in His essence, His attributes and His acts. His dominion is a perfect dominion, with no deficiency in any respect, whatever it may be like.

Some people said: His bringing His creation into being in the way it exists is more perfect than bringing it into being in any other way, and better than its existing otherwise. Whatever evil is in it

is relative evil, evil in relation to some things and not others; it is not absolute evil, such that its non-existence would be better than its existence in every respect — rather, its existence is better than its non-existence. He said:

This is the meaning of His words, “In His hand is the good” [Āl ʿImrān 3:26], and of the Prophet's words ﷺ, “And evil is not to You” — meaning that pure evil, whose non-existence is better than its existence, does not exist in Your dominion.

For Allah the Exalted brought His creation into being as His wisdom and justice require; He singled out some of His creation for grace and left others to justice, because of the far-reaching wisdom He has in that.

This is open to question, and it conflicts with what is in the hadith: that if all creation had the righteousness and taqwā of the most perfect of His creation, that would not add anything to His dominion, not even the size of a gnat's wing;

and if they had the wickedness of the most deficient of His creation, that would take nothing from His dominion. This shows that His dominion is perfect, whatever it may be like; it neither increases nor is perfected by acts of obedience, nor decreases through sins, and nothing affects it.

These words also show that the root of taqwā and wickedness is the heart: when the heart is righteous and God-fearing, the limbs are righteous; and when the heart is wicked, the limbs are wicked. As the Prophet ﷺ said: “Taqwā is here,” pointing to his chest.
His words: “My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, your humans and your jinn, stood on a single plain and asked of Me, and I gave every person what he asked,

that would diminish what I have no more than a needle diminishes the sea when it is put into it.” What is meant by this is to mention the perfection of His power, Glorified is He, and the perfection of His dominion, and that His dominion and His treasuries are never exhausted
nor diminished by giving, even if He gave the first and the last, of jinn and humans, all they asked of Him in a single gathering.
In this there is encouragement for creation to ask Him and bring their needs to Him. In the two Ṣaḥīḥs, from Abū Hurayrah, the Prophet ﷺ said:
“Allah's hand is full; no spending diminishes it; it pours out night and day. Do you see what He has spent since He created the heavens and the earth?
It has not diminished what is in His right hand.”

In Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, from Abū Hurayrah, the Prophet ﷺ said: “When one of you supplicates, let him not say, ‘O Allah, forgive me if You wish’; rather, let him be firm in his request and make his longing great, for nothing is too great for Allah.”
Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī said: When you call on Allah, aim high in what you ask, for nothing exhausts what He has; and when you call on Him, be firm, for no one can compel Allah.
In some of the Israelite reports: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: Is anyone other than I hoped in for hardships, when hardships are in My hand and I am the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of all?
Is anyone other than I hoped in, and his door knocked on in the early mornings, when the keys of the treasuries are in My hand and My door is open to whoever calls on Me?
Who is it that hoped in Me in some misfortune and I failed him?
Or who is it that hoped in Me for something great and I cut off his hope?
Or who is it that knocked at My door and I did not open it for him?
I am the goal of all hopes; how then can hopes stop short of Me?
Am I a miser, that My servant should think Me miserly?
Do not this world and the Hereafter, and all nobility and bounty, belong to Me?
What then keeps those who hope from hoping in Me?

If I gathered the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth and then gave each one of them what I gave them all, and brought each one of them his hope, that would not diminish My dominion by so much as the limb of an ant. How could a dominion of which I am the Sustainer be diminished?
So woe to those who despair of My mercy, and woe to whoever disobeys Me and leaps upon what I have made sacred.
His words, “That would diminish what I have no more than a needle diminishes the sea when it is put into it,” affirm that what He has does not diminish at all, as the Exalted said:
“What you have will be exhausted, but what Allah has will remain” [al-Naḥl 16:96]. For when a needle is dipped into the sea and then taken out, nothing of the sea is diminished by it;

and likewise if one supposes that a sparrow, say, drank from it, that would not diminish the sea at all. That is why al-Khaḍir struck this parable for Mūsā (peace be upon them both) concerning their knowledge in relation to the knowledge of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.
This is because the sea is constantly fed by the waters of the world and its flowing rivers, so however much is taken from it, nothing diminishes it,

because what feeds it is more than what is taken from it. The same is true of the food of Paradise and everything in it: it is never exhausted, as the Exalted said: “And abundant fruit, neither cut off nor forbidden” [al-Wāqiʿah 56:32–33].

It has come that “whenever a fruit is plucked, another like it returns in its place” — and it is narrated, “two like it” — so it never diminishes. This is attested by the words of the Prophet ﷺ in the sermon of the eclipse:

“I was shown Paradise, and I reached for a bunch of grapes from it; had I taken it, you would have eaten from it as long as the world remained.” Both recorded it in the two Ṣaḥīḥs from the hadith of Ibn ʿAbbās,
and Imam Aḥmad recorded it from the hadith of Jābir, in the wording: “Had I brought it to you, all who are between heaven and earth would have eaten from it without diminishing it at all.”

Likewise, the flesh of the birds that the people of Paradise eat is replaced and returns as it was, alive, with nothing of it diminished. This has been narrated from the Prophet ﷺ by routes that contain weakness, and Kaʿb said it.
It is also narrated from Abū Umāmah al-Bāhilī as his own words; Abū Umāmah said: Likewise the drink: one drinks until his breath runs out, and then it returns to its place.

One of the righteous scholars was seen in a dream some time after his death, and he said: Since I left you I have eaten only part of a chick. Did you not know that the food of Paradise is never exhausted?

In the hadith recorded by al-Tirmidhī and Ibn Mājah He made clear the reason why what Allah has does not diminish through giving, in His words: “That is because I am Generous, Rich and Glorious; I do what I will. My giving is a word and My punishment is a word;

My command for a thing, when I will it, is only to say to it: Be — and it is.” This is like His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: “His command, when He wills a thing, is only to say to it: Be — and it is” [Yā Sīn 36:82]; and the words of the Exalted: “Our word to a thing, when We will it, is only that We say to it: Be — and it is” [al-Naḥl 16:40].
In the Musnad of al-Bazzār, with a chain open to question, from the hadith of Abū Hurayrah, the Prophet ﷺ said:

“The treasuries of Allah are the word: when He wills a thing, He says to it: Be — and it is.” So when He, Glorified is He, wills anything — giving, punishment or anything else — He says to it: Be, and it is. How could this conceivably diminish?

Likewise, when He wills to create something, He says to it: Be — and it is, as He said: “Indeed, the likeness of ʿĪsā with Allah is that of Ādam: He created him from dust, then said to him: Be — and he was” [Āl ʿImrān 3:59].

In some of the Israelite reports: Allah the Exalted revealed to Mūsā (peace be upon him): Mūsā, never fear anyone but Me so long as authority is Mine — and My authority is everlasting and never ends. Mūsā, never be anxious about My provision so long as My treasuries are full —

and My treasuries are full and will never run out. Mūsā, do not seek company in anyone but Me so long as you find Me a companion to you — and whenever you seek Me you will find Me. Mūsā, do not feel safe from My plan until you have crossed the Bridge into Paradise. And someone said:
Never humble yourself before a created being out of greed, / for that will do harm to your religion;
ask Allah for provision from what is in His treasuries, / for they lie only between the kāf and the nūn [of kun, “Be”].

His words, “My servants, it is only your deeds that I record for you and then repay you for in full,” mean that He, Glorified is He, records the deeds of His servants and then repays them in full by recompensing them for them. This is like His words: “Whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it” [al-Zalzalah 99:7–8]; His words:

“And they will find what they did present, and your Lord wrongs no one” [al-Kahf 18:49]; His words: “The Day every soul will find what it has done of good brought forward, and what it has done of evil — it will wish there were a great distance between it and that” [Āl ʿImrān 3:30];
and His words: “The Day Allah will raise them all and inform them of what they did; Allah has recorded it, while they forgot it” [al-Mujādilah 58:6].

His words, “And then repay you for in full”: the apparent meaning is repaying them in full on the Day of Resurrection, as the Exalted said: “And you will only be paid your rewards in full on the Day of Resurrection” [Āl ʿImrān 3:185]. It may also mean that He repays His servants in full the recompense of their deeds in this world and the Hereafter, as in His words: “Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it” [al-Nisāʾ 4:123].

It has been narrated that the Prophet ﷺ explained this as meaning that the believers are recompensed for their bad deeds in this world, while their good deeds are stored up for them in the Hereafter, where they are paid their rewards in full.
As for the disbeliever, the reward for his good deeds is hastened to him in this world, and his bad deeds are stored up for him, to be punished for in the Hereafter.
Repaying deeds in full means repaying their recompense in full, whether good or evil. Evil is recompensed with its like, without increase, unless Allah pardons it;

and as for good, each good deed is multiplied ten times, up to seven hundred times, up to many multiples whose extent none knows but Allah, as the Mighty and Majestic said: “Only the patient will be given their reward in full, without measure” [al-Zumar 39:10].

His words, “So whoever finds good, let him praise Allah; and whoever finds otherwise, let him blame no one but himself,” indicate that all good is from Allah, a grace from Him to His servant that the servant has not earned,

and all evil comes from the son of Ādam himself, from following his own whims, as the Mighty and Majestic said: “Whatever good befalls you is from Allah, and whatever evil befalls you is from yourself” [al-Nisāʾ 4:79]. ʿAlī (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Let no servant hope in anyone but his Lord,

and let him fear nothing but his own sin. When Allah, Glorified is He, wills to grant a servant success and guidance, He helps him and enables him to obey Him, and that is a grace from Him; and when He wills to forsake a servant, He leaves him to himself and lets him go his own way,

so that Satan leads him astray because of his heedlessness of the remembrance of Allah, and he follows his whims, and his affair becomes all excess — and that is justice from Him. For the proof stands against the servant through the sending down of the Book and the sending of the Messenger, so that no one has any argument against Allah after the messengers.
His words after this, “So whoever finds good, let him praise Allah; and whoever finds otherwise, let him blame no one but himself”: if what is meant is whoever finds that in this world,
then he is commanded to praise Allah for the recompense of righteous deeds that has been hastened to him in this world, as He said:

“Whoever does righteous deeds, male or female, while being a believer — We will surely give him a good life, and We will surely give them their reward according to the best of what they used to do” [al-Naḥl 16:97]; and he is commanded to blame himself for the sins it committed, whose consequences he has found in this world, as the Exalted said:

“And We will surely make them taste the nearer punishment short of the greater punishment, so that perhaps they will return” [al-Sajdah 32:21]. So when an affliction befalls the believer in this world, he turns on himself with blame,
and that leads him to return to Allah through repentance and seeking forgiveness. In the Musnad and the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd, the Prophet ﷺ said:

“When the believer is struck by illness and then Allah heals him of it, it is an expiation for his past sins and an admonition to him for the rest of his life. But when the hypocrite falls ill and is then restored to health, he is like a camel whose owners hobbled it and then released it: it does not know why they hobbled it or why they released it.”

Salmān al-Fārisī said: The Muslim is afflicted, and it is an expiation for what is past and a chance to make amends in what remains; while the disbeliever is afflicted, and his likeness is that of a camel that is released and does not know why it was released, and hobbled and does not know why it was hobbled.

If what is meant is whoever finds good or otherwise in the Hereafter, then it is a statement that those who find good in the Hereafter will praise Allah for it, and that whoever finds otherwise will blame himself when blame will be of no use to him.

The wording would then be that of a command but its meaning a statement, like his words ﷺ, “Whoever lies about me deliberately, let him take his seat in the Fire,” which means that whoever lies about him will take his seat in the Fire.
Allah the Exalted has told of the people of Paradise that they praise Allah for what He has provided them of His bounty. He said:

“And We will remove whatever rancour is in their breasts; rivers will flow beneath them, and they will say: Praise be to Allah, who guided us to this; we would never have been guided had Allah not guided us” [al-Aʿrāf 7:43];
and He said: “And they will say: Praise be to Allah, who has fulfilled His promise to us and made us inherit the land, so that we settle in Paradise wherever we wish” [al-Zumar 39:74]; and He said:

“And they will say: Praise be to Allah, who has removed grief from us; indeed, our Lord is Forgiving, Appreciative — who has settled us in the Abode of Permanence out of His bounty; no weariness touches us in it, nor any fatigue” [Fāṭir 35:34–35].
And He told of the people of the Fire that they blame themselves and loathe themselves with the utmost loathing. The Exalted said:

“And Satan will say when the matter has been decided: Indeed, Allah promised you the promise of truth, and I promised you and broke my promise to you. I had no authority over you except that I called you and you responded to me. So do not blame me, but blame yourselves” [Ibrāhīm 14:22];

and the Exalted said: “Indeed, those who disbelieved will be called out to: Allah's loathing [of you] was greater than your loathing of yourselves, when you were called to faith and you disbelieved” [Ghāfir 40:10].
The righteous Salaf used to exert themselves in righteous deeds,
wary of the self-blame for falling short that comes when deeds have come to an end.
In al-Tirmidhī's collection, from Abū Hurayrah, as marfūʿ (attributed to the Prophet ﷺ):
“No one dies without regret: if he did good, he regrets not having done more; and if he did evil, he regrets not having made amends.”

Masrūq was told: If only you would cut back on some of the effort you make! He said: By Allah, if someone came to me and told me that He would not punish me, I would still exert myself in worship. He was asked: How is that?

He said: So that my soul will excuse me, if I enter the Fire, from blaming it. Has it not reached you concerning the words of the Exalted, “And I swear by the self-reproaching soul” [al-Qiyāmah 75:2], that they blamed themselves only when they had come to Hell,
and the guards of Hell (al-zabāniyah) seized them, and they were barred from what they desired, their hopes were cut off, mercy was lifted from them, and each of them set about blaming himself?
ʿĀmir ibn ʿAbd Qays used to say: By Allah, I will exert myself, and again, by Allah, I will exert myself; if I am saved, it will be by Allah's mercy, and if not, I will not blame myself.

Ziyād, the freed slave of Ibn ʿAyyāsh, used to say to Ibn al-Munkadir and Ṣafwān ibn Sulaym: Earnestness, earnestness! Caution, caution! If the matter turns out as we hope, what you have done will be extra; and if not, you will not blame yourselves.
Muṭarrif ibn ʿAbdillāh used to say: Exert yourselves in deeds. If the matter is as we hope from Allah's mercy and pardon, we will have degrees in Paradise;

and if the matter is severe, as we fear and dread, we will not say, “Our Lord, take us out; we will do righteous deeds, other than what we used to do” [Fāṭir 35:37]; we will say: We did act, and it was of no use to us.
